input.quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by Customer to Vendor for any dependency delay, with no materiality threshold, notice requirement, or aggregate cap — exposure that can quickly exceed the contract value and is triggered by minor administrative slippage. Our playbook position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer (service credits or LDs running to us are fine, and none appear elsewhere in the document). We therefore delete the Customer-payable LD and give Vendor schedule relief plus documented out-of-pocket costs instead.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: Customer shall not be liable for liquidated damages, penalties, or similar pre-agreed sums under this Agreement. If Customer delays in providing a dependency identified in the applicable Order Form, Vendor's affected performance dates and service-level obligations are extended to the extent of that delay, and Vendor's sole remedy is that schedule relief together with reimbursement of reasonable, documented, unavoidable costs Vendor incurs as a direct result of the delay after written notice to Customer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages payable by Customer, as our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us. In its place Vendor receives schedule relief and documented out-of-pocket costs for any dependency delay, which addresses the underlying risk without a punitive daily charge.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages in §7.6 and replace with excused-performance relief for Vendor.
